name: Why Driveway Repairs Fail and Crack Again

mainEntity.name: What causes concrete or asphalt driveways in Los Angeles County to crack again after repair?
mainEntity.text: What causes concrete or asphalt driveways in Los Angeles County to crack again after repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repeat cracking usually means the underlying problem was not corrected. Common causes include a weak or poorly compacted base, water intrusion from poor grading, soil expansion and shrinkage, tree root pressure, and traffic loads that exceed the driveway’s design. In Los Angeles County, localized settlement and runoff from slopes or hardscape can make these issues worse. A good contractor should explain whether the cracks are reflective, structural, or caused by drainage. If water is pooling or running under the slab, sealing the crack alone will not last. Effective repair may require base stabilization, localized slab replacement, proper joint treatment, or redirecting water away from the driveway.
acceptedAnswer.description: Driveways usually crack again when the underlying base is unstable, drainage sends water under the pavement, or the repair was only cosmetic. Temperature changes, soil movement, tree roots, and heavy loads can also reopen cracks. A lasting repair addresses the cause, not just the visible surface damage.
